title: What If a Plane's Door Blew Off Mid-Flight? It Did in 2024, With 177 People Aboard

scenes.text: What if part of a plane's wall blew off mid-flight? In 2024 it did. Two seats saved everyone.
January 5, 2024. Six minutes after takeoff from Portland, at 16,000 feet, a door-sized panel of a Boeing 737 MAX rips away.
Air roars out. Phones, headsets and a teenager's shirt are sucked into the sky. Oxygen masks drop.
The two seats right beside the gap? Empty. Of 177 people aboard, only seven seats were free, and two were those.
Twenty minutes after takeoff, the jet is back on the ground. Eight minor injuries. A phone that fell 16,000 feet still works.
Investigators found the panel had been refitted with its four bolts missing. Minutes later, at cruising altitude, it could have been a tragedy.

description:
What if a plane's door blew off in flight? On 5 January 2024, Alaska Airlines Flight 1282, a Boeing 737 MAX 9 with 177 people aboard, lost a door plug panel about six minutes after takeoff from Portland, at roughly 16,000 feet and over 400 mph.
The decompression pulled phones, headsets and a teenager's shirt out of the cabin and dropped the oxygen masks; the two seats next to the hole were empty. The plane landed back in Portland about 20 minutes after takeoff with eight minor injuries, and a phone that fell from the aircraft was found still working. The NTSB found the panel had been reinstalled without its four retaining bolts and said a blowout at cruising altitude could have been a tragedy.
